newsitem.title: HONG KONG: First Pacific says 1996 core profits up.
newsitem.headline: First Pacific says 1996 core profits up.

text.p: First Pacific Co Ltd said on Monday that strong performances in all four of its core businesses boosted core recurrent earnings for 1996 by 32 percent, despite a drop in net profit after exceptionals.
The company said attributable profit before net exceptional items totalled HK$1.57 billion (US$202 million) in calendar 1996, up from HK$1.19 billion a year earlier.
Turnover rose 34 percent to HK$54.8 billion.

"By any measure, 1996 was a year of significant achievement for us. Despite difficulties in a number of economies where we operate, recurrent earnings rose significantly with improved contributions at each of out four core businesses," managing director Manuel Pangilinan said in a statement.
Pangilinan added he remained confident of the company's prospects for 1997.
The blue chip conglomerate posted a 20.5 percent drop at the net profit level to US$204.2 million (HK$1.59 billion) for 1996 from US$257 million in 1995.
The net includes an exceptional loss of US$92.6 million from the reorganisation and rationalisation of subsidiaries and associated companies and provision for investments.
This was partly offset by an exceptional gain of US$76.8 million from the dilution and disposal of shareholdings in subsidiaries and associated companies.
In 1995, First Pacific reported an exceptional gain of US$86.1 million.
First Pacific mainly engages in marketing and distribution, telecommunications, property and banking.
"The marketing and distribution business benefited from the strength of both Dutch-based Hagemeyer and ASEAN-based operations," Pangilinan said.
First Pacific owns a controlling stake in Hagemeyer NV, which posted net profit of 285.2 million guilders in 1996, up 47.5 percent from 1995.
The sector contributed to profit before exceptionals of about HK$843 million in 1996, up 23 percent from a year earlier, while turnover rose 35 percent to HK$48.7 billion.
First Pacific said it had made good progress in its telecommunications business in China, India, Indonesia, Hong Kong and the Philippines.

Its Hong Kong cellular phone arm Pacific Link Communications Ltd contributed HK$453 million to profits, up 38 percent from a year earlier, although revenue at the arm eased four percent to HK$1.97 billion in 1996.
Subscriber numbers increased only eight percent to 240,000 following the previous year's 150 percent jump, it said
Smart Communications, the company's major mobile phone operations in the Philippines held by Metro Pacific Corp, saw it contribution jump 94 percent to HK$74 million.
Its cellular subscriber base climbed 173 percent to 310,000, giving it 39 percent of the total market.

First Pacific said its property sector contributed profits before exceptionals of HK$277 million, up 25 percent, and the banking sector contributed profits before exceptionals of HK$207 million, up 71 percent.
